title: pull_request_target workflows: key the concurrency group on PR number with cancel-in-progress false, not run_id or github.ref
answers: Why do the pull_request_target labeling, size, approval or close workflows run 4 to 5 times for the same PR?
How do I make a new pull_request_target workflow run only once per PR in the queue?
Why does github.ref not work as a concurrency key for pull_request_target workflows?
Where is the concurrency group for the PR size and community label automation defined?
body:
Path: the top-level `concurrency:` block of the pull_request_target workflows in .github/workflows (advice, approval, auto-close-pr, cancel, cherry-picks-warn, closing-pr, community-label, patch, pr-size, route-ready-issue-pr), which handle per-PR comments, labels, size, approval and close automation.
Rule: group these runs with `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}` and `cancel-in-progress: false`. Under pull_request_target, github.ref resolves to the default branch, so it cannot separate PRs; the PR number does. GitHub keeps at most one running and one pending run per group, so repeated events for one PR collapse instead of piling up.
Symptom: the same automation for one PR ran 4 to 5 times, each run repeating its work.
Constraints: concurrency is resolved before the job-level `if:`, so a run that will no-op could cancel a useful in-flight run; that is why cancel-in-progress is false. A later run still replaces a pending one in the group, so only use this for workflows whose events do the same kind of work. route-ready-issue-pr adds the team-review label with GITHUB_TOKEN, which emits no label event, so cancelling its in-flight run can strand reviewer assignment.
applies: Adding or editing concurrency blocks in pull_request_target workflows under .github/workflows that should coalesce runs per PR.
says: Automated labeling and size checks run multiple times repeatedly for the same pull request.
Pull request triage automation triggers four or five times on a single change.
Stop duplicate approval and close automation from running repeatedly on one pull request.
Coalesce redundant pull request workflow runs so pending jobs collapse instead of piling up.
Team reviewer assignment gets stranded when pull request routing jobs are cancelled.
search: Top-level concurrency blocks in .github/workflows for pull_request_target workflows must be keyed on ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} with cancel-in-progress: false rather than github.ref or run_id. Because github.ref resolves to the default branch under pull_request_target, grouping by PR number collapses repeated events into at most one running and one pending run per PR. The cancel-in-progress setting must remain false because concurrency resolves before job-level if: conditions, which would otherwise allow no-op runs to cancel active work and potentially strand reviewer assignment in route-ready-issue-pr.
